fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**

I cannot tell. At the size and brightness shown it is black — not dark, black.

Under a hard gamma lift there is something there, and it is still not a material: the south run (x 57–722, y 774–825) is a **plain flat grey plane crossed by evenly spaced vertical dark lines**, nothing else. The north and west runs are **flat grey rectangles with a horizontal banding**. If I had to say what a hand would land on, the honest answer is "a grey surface." Not stone, not brick, not rock, not timber. Grey.
fields.Q1_WHY:
Measured over the south wall band (x 100–700, y 790–825): mean luminance **8.88/255**, standard deviation **1.73**, total range **7 levels** (min 6, max 13), **30 unique colours in 21,000 pixels**. West band (x 5–55, y 300–700): mean 8.65, range 18. East band (x 725–748): mean 7.20, range 8. Brightest wall region in the entire frame — the north course directly above the figure, x 340–480, y 200–234 — is mean **13.9**, peak **30**. For scale, the lit ground beside the figure runs mean 108, peak 231, range 191. The standing structure is rendered at roughly **8% of the ground's luminance and 4% of its contrast range**. There is no material information in 7–18 levels of near-black.

---
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR A FLAT PATTERN AROUND THE EDGE?**

**A flat pattern around the edge.**

What decided it: I looked for the three things that make a top-down wall read as mass, and none are present.

- **No cast shadow.** Nothing darkens on the ground side of any wall run. At x=400 the boundary is y 773→774: `(5,5,5)` → `(10,9,10)`. The step is 5 levels and it goes the *wrong way* — the wall is **brighter** than the ground immediately adjacent to it. A solid mass under a point light does not brighten as it recedes from the light.
- **No top face vs. side face.** A lifted read of the south band (`band_south.png`, y 770–830 full width) shows one continuous flat plane. No lit cap, no darker flank, no bevel, no lip. The vertical lines through it are 2px seams on the same flat value.
- **No occlusion.** The north corridor flanks (x 314–375 and x 441–502, y 0–200) are the same value top to bottom, with nothing behind them and nothing in front.

It is bounded by a change of colour of about six luminance levels, not by anything with thickness.

---
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**

Four places, all the same event.

South, at **x=400, y=773/774** — the sharpest one. Ground values descend 13, 10, 8, 6, 5, 5 across y 765–773, then at y=774 jump to 10 and hold at 9–10 for the next fifty rows. **The whole transition is one pixel.** What changes across it: luminance goes *up* by 5, and the noise stops — variance collapses from the ground's speckle to a near-constant field.

Same at x=690: y 773 is `(2,2,3)`, y 774 is `(6,6,8)`, then a second step to `(9,9,12)` at y 778. Two 1px steps, 4 pixels apart, total delta 7 levels.

West, at **y=470, x=54/55**: `(9,9,12)` → `(3,3,3)`. One pixel, 6 levels down.

North, at **x=250, y=229/230**: `(10,10,12)` → `(2,2,3)`. One pixel.

So: the ground stops at a hard one-pixel line with a five-to-seven-level luminance step and no transition zone at all. On a phone that line does not exist.

---
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**

**NOTHING.**

I searched every wall run at 4x and 10x for a pin, a tie, a brace, a prop, a lashing, a patch — anything spanning a joint or bearing on anything. There is exactly one candidate in the whole frame: **x 135–147, y 195–228**, a vertical bar with three horizontal cross-bars (`stem.png`). It could be a ladder, a driven spike, or a bracket. It is drawn in mid-grey on mid-grey, it spans nothing, it bears on nothing, and at 1:1 its pixels read RGB ~5 — it is invisible. It is one object in roughly 2,400 pixels of wall run.

There is nothing I could cut. Nothing would fall down.

---
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR AN IMAGE THAT WAS REPEATED?**

**Repeated.**

Autocorrelation along the north band (y 200–231, x 60–720) returns peaks at lags **24, 30, 34** (r ≈ 0.51) and **59** (r ≈ 0.45) — a stamped cell of about 30px with a 60px pair. The north corridor's two flanks (x 314–375 and x 441–502) carry the same horizontal banding at the same vertical period, mirrored across the passage, unbroken from y=0 to y=200. The south run is the clearest case: one flat value, seams at a fixed pitch, all the way across 665 pixels with no variation, no interruption, no corner treatment, no course break.

Nothing in it responds to anything else in it. Corners are the same as runs. The wall next to the passage is the same as the wall in the middle of nowhere.

---
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED IN A COMMERCIAL GAME?**

**NO.**

And separately: it is not merely competent either. There is no judgement to assess. The standing structure is not underlit — it is absent. A shipped game does not render its bounding geometry at a mean of 8/255 with a 7-level range while the ground beside it runs to 231. This is a lighting/authoring failure, not a style.

---
fields.Q7:
WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE ON THE STANDING SURFACES AT 1:1?**

**Legible at 1:1 on the standing surfaces: nothing.** All four runs are blank black. I could not distinguish wall from void from the unlit ground by eye. This does not change with distance from the figure in any useful way — the nearest wall (west, x=55) is ~180px from the figure and reads luminance 14; the north wall at its best point reads 14 mean / 30 peak. Nothing anywhere crosses into legibility.

**Only appears under magnification and gamma lift:** the rectangular block courses of the north and west runs; the horizontal banding of the corridor flanks; the vertical seam pitch of the south run; the ladder/pin at x 135–147, y 195–228; the recessed rectangle at **x 182–247, y 455–517** (the one wall-adjacent feature that sits inside the lit radius — and even lifted it is a flat darker rectangle with internal divisions, no lip, no shadow, no thickness).

Every one of those took hunting with a gamma curve and 4–10x zoom. That is hunting, not seeing.
fields.Q8:
IS THERE ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**

Yes — the **vertical seam lines in the south run**, at approximately x=232, 267, and repeating on a ~55–60px pitch across the full width at y 774–825. They are the only thing with any rhythm to it, and once seen they are unmistakably a fixed-interval stamp. There is no variation between one and the next.

Second: the **mirror symmetry of the north corridor flanks**. The band at x 314–375 and the band at x 441–502 carry identical horizontal courses at identical heights from y=0 to y=200. Both edges of the passage are the same picture.

---
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**

**Empty space — and not in a way that reads as fiction.** It is a single flat fill. The region x 0–300, y 0–190 contains **exactly one colour, RGB(1,1,2), across 57,000 pixels, standard deviation 0.00**. Same value, same zero variance, in the north-east region x 520–740, y 60–190. It is not more of the same stuff, it is not a room I cannot see into, it is not something I cannot name. It is a solid rectangle of `#010102`.

The problem this creates: the wall runs measure mean 7–9 and the void measures 1.3. **Seven levels separate "wall" from "nothing."** Below the just-noticeable difference on a phone in any ambient light. The structure and the void are the same thing to a player.

---
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH FROM A DEAD END WITHOUT WALKING INTO IT?**

**No.** I found the gap — the passage runs north from the room at **x ≈ 376–440, y 0–235**, flanked by wall at x 314–375 and x 441–502. I found it only in the gamma-lifted image.

What settles it is a measurement, not an impression. Over y 60–200:

- passage ground (x 378–438): mean luminance **7.70**
- flanking wall (x 320–370): mean luminance **8.35**

**The wall is brighter than the passage.** Scanning across at y=100 from x=300 to x=520, every single value is between 4 and 10 — void, wall, passage, wall, void, all one undifferentiated band. The only marks distinguishing the opening are 3-level dips at x=380 and x=436, which are the seam pixels.

There is no read here at all. Not a weak read — an inverted one. A player would have to walk into it.

---
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**

Nothing has happened to it, and nothing has been done to it. Under lift, every run is uniform end to end: no chipping, no spalling, no settlement, no gap, no course out of line, no repair, no patch, no replaced block, no stain, no accretion. The south run is a single flat value for 665 pixels. The corner where west meets south is treated exactly as the middle of a run.

I read this from the variance figures more than from any single look: sd 1.73 over the whole south band, 2.42 over the east, 30 unique colours in 21,000 pixels. Damage, wear and repair are variance. There isn't any.

For a place in continuous heavy use since before anyone's records begin, held for four hundred years by a company that repairs everything with rope and driven pins and does not care how it looks — this structure has never been touched by anyone, ever. It is the one thing in the frame that has no history.

---
fields.CULL:
Walls render at mean 8/255 against a void at 1/255 — structure is invisible and indistinguishable from nothing.

---
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Raise the standing structure's lit response so the nearest wall to the light source reads at minimum 60–80/255 with a 40+ level internal range; currently the brightest wall pixel in the frame is 30 and the mean is 14.
- Separate wall from void by at least 25 luminance levels at all lit distances, and give the void beyond the walls a value or texture that is not a single flat `#010102` fill — right now 7 levels separate structure from nothing.
- Add a cast shadow on the ground side of every wall run, 6–10px, so the boundary reads as mass. At x=400/y=774 the wall is currently *brighter* than the ground it meets.
- Make the north passage (x 376–440) read as an opening without walking into it: it is currently 0.65 luminance levels *darker* than the wall beside it. Light spill up the throat, or a distinct threshold treatment at y≈235.
- Break the repeat: the south run is one flat value with seams on a fixed ~57px pitch across its full width, and the two corridor flanks are mirror-identical from y 0–200. Add course breaks, a repair or two — rope, driven pins, salvaged timber — and corner treatment that differs from a run.

---
